blocks.text: Zero Trust Browser lets admins decide whether users can access different domains while in isolation. If the Original URL feature is enabled, Internet & SaaS (ZIA) evaluates link redirects for users. If the link leads to a domain different than the one accessed at the beginning of isolation, the new page renders on the user's local browser, outside the isolation session.

For example, if a user in isolation clicks a link that redirects to a new page in the same tab, the tab loads the new page, and the tab is no longer part of an isolated session. As a result, the web page appears without the look and feel of the isolated session. However, by clicking the Back button on the browser, the user can return to the prior page and, in doing so, return to the ongoing isolated session. Similarly, if a user in isolation clicks a link that redirects to a different domain in a new window or tab, that new window or tab opens outside the isolated session.
Admins can enable the Original URL option per Internet & SaaS isolation profile. To learn more, see Creating Isolation Profiles for Internet & SaaS.
